what: SK Telecom is South Korea's largest mobile operator. It sells phone subscriptions, fixed broadband through its SK Broadband arm, and has been building data centre and AI services.
customers: South Korean households and businesses, on mobile and broadband subscriptions.
money: data centres, cloud and AI services
moat: A network and spectrum in a market with three operators, and the largest subscriber base in a country where almost everyone already has a phone.
risks: Korean mobile is saturated, so growth has to come from somewhere other than subscriptions
A 2025 data breach of subscriber identity information led to customer losses and penalties
The Korean government periodically pressures carriers to cut tariffs
opportunities: 12.4 times earnings and 6.4 times free cash flow with $1.9B of free cash flow
$1.4B of cash against only $68M of debt at the parent level
Data centre and AI services grow from a small base in a country short of capacity
watch: Mobile subscriber trends after the breach, and data centre revenue.
